Every action explained
Start inside a small enabled area on the left, right, top, or bottom edge.

1. Open a zone, turn it on, and assign a gesture action. The right side has a starting setup; the other zones can be enabled when needed.

2. Set thickness, length, position, and orientation. Drag the zone preview to move it. Two zones on each side can use different actions.

3. The three bottom shortcut zones sit above the system navigation area. Enabling them replaces the single bottom EdgeGo zone.

4. Only gestures that begin inside a configured zone are handled. The system navigation area and respected app exclusions remain available.
One, two, or three quick taps select one assigned action.

1. Assign Tap, Double tap, and Triple tap separately in a zone. Touch and release inside that same zone without moving far.

2. When a higher tap count is assigned, EdgeGo waits for the multiple tap interval before choosing the action. A triple tap runs its own action once.

3. Use the same finger in the same area for the whole sequence. Moving into a swipe or adding another finger ends tap recognition.

4. A tap count set to None does nothing. Touches outside the small tap zones continue to the screen normally.
Swipe along an edge, inward, or diagonally to select an action.

1. On a side edge, swipe up or down along the edge, or pull inward, diagonally up, or diagonally down. At the top and bottom, slide left or right or pull inward.

2. Move past Swipe distance. The action icon and label show the selected direction. Release to run a single action.

3. With continuous adjustment enabled, volume and brightness up/down start adjusting after the swipe is recognized. Keep your finger down for repeated adjustment, then release to stop.

4. If a direction has a different hold or extended action, complete that selection first. This keeps each assigned gesture available.
Pause at the edge or after a swipe; keep holding continuous controls.

1. For Long press, touch the zone and stay still until Hold delay passes. For Swipe-and-hold, swipe past the distance threshold and pause at the end.

2. The action indicator changes when the hold is recognized. Assign volume or brightness up/down to a hold gesture to keep increasing or decreasing while your finger stays down.

3. Release or return to the starting edge to end adjustment. The adjustment interval controls the rate; brightness changes smoothly between steps.

4. Run hold actions on release applies to single actions. Continuous controls operate while the finger is held. Slider actions follow subsequent finger movement.
A longer swipe selects a separate extended action.

1. Assign an Extended action for a direction, then move farther than Extended swipe distance. This distance stays at least 50 percent longer than Swipe distance. Watch the selected action label change.

2. Release to run that action, or pause for the assigned hold action. The hold selection takes precedence when it becomes ready.

3. An ordinary continuous control waits when the same direction has a different extended action, so the longer gesture can still be selected.

4. Use distinct distance thresholds and direction stability to reduce accidental changes. Return to the starting edge to cancel.
Stop an adjustment, pause an edge, and leave system gestures available.

1. Return near the starting point before release to cancel when Return to edge to cancel is enabled. This also stops continuous adjustment.

2. Tap through pauses the originating zone for its configured duration. Pause EdgeGo temporarily pauses the whole feature; the Quick Settings tile controls whether it is enabled.

3. Keep app gesture exclusion protection enabled and use narrow zones. Bottom zones stay above system navigation. Keyboard, lock screen, launcher, fullscreen, GameSpace, and touch exploration have pause controls.

4. A second finger, screen state change, or user switch cancels an active gesture. Hiding an indicator only changes its visibility; pause or disable the zone to stop input handling.
Tune touch priority, timing, repeat protection, and automatic pauses.

1. Use Behavior and timing to set swipe distances, tap tolerance, hold delay, multiple tap interval, direction stability, gesture time limit, and accidental repeat protection.

2. Configured side zones have priority inside their bounds. Respect app gesture exclusions protects app edge interactions. Keep edges above keyboard is optional.

3. Choose when to pause on the lock screen, launcher, fullscreen apps, GameSpace, or touch exploration. GameSpace and touch exploration protection start enabled.

4. Sync left and right actions copies the selected side mapping. Zone positions and sizes can still be configured separately.
Match edge indicators and panel colors to the ROM theme.

1. Choose soft fade, clear bounds, or pill indicators, then set opacity and each edge color. A zone can hide its own indicator.

2. Use system accent and tinted surfaces to follow the ROM palette. Choose system, light, or dark panels, or supply custom light and dark accents.

3. Separate sync controls apply the accent to sliders, edges, waves, bubbles, pie surfaces, and Quick Tools. Hidden idle or fullscreen indicators still recognize gestures.

4. For less distraction, lower indicator opacity or enable idle hiding. Disable a zone when you want its touch area removed.
Spring motion, changing shapes, action previews, and vibration.

1. Choose wave, bubble, or minimal gesture feedback. Enable action labels, action icons, and app icons to see what will run before release.

2. Spring responsiveness and damping tune panel and button motion. System animation settings are respected, including disabled animations.

3. Set vibration strength and a single or double pulse. Direction feedback confirms a new sector; holding confirms a hold action.

4. The Vibrate switch in each zone can disable its feedback. Use Try vibration to check the chosen pattern.
Move rounded floating controls and choose outside touch behavior.

1. Drag a panel title to move it. Remember panel positions restores the location; Reset panel positions returns panels to their starting placement.

2. Panel size, corner radius, theme, opacity, and idle timeout control the appearance and lifetime. Panels stay within safe screen and keyboard bounds.

3. Outside taps can close a panel or pass through according to its settings. System Back closes an open panel before navigating away.

4. Blur is available behind ordinary panels. Macro recording, cursor, touchpad, and scrolling controls keep the screen clear for interaction.
One swipe or swipe-and-hold can keep changing volume or brightness.

1. Continuous swipe adjustment is enabled by default. Assign media, ringtone, or notification volume up/down, or brightness up/down, to a swipe or hold gesture.

2. A recognized gesture applies its first step and keeps adjusting while the finger stays down, including when it is held still. Moving farther adds adjustment. Release or cancel to stop.

3. The adjustment interval sets repeated step speed; slider sensitivity sets movement response. Brightness step sets the brightness rate. A distinct hold or extended mapping waits for that selection.

4. Volume slider and Brightness slider follow your finger along the selected horizontal or vertical orientation. Active audio following selects call or ringing volume when appropriate. Brightness is saved on release.
Split inward pulls into one to seven stable directions.

1. Enable Custom pull sectors and choose the number of sectors. Each sector gets ordinary, hold, and extended actions in the zone gesture list.

2. Drag the divider dots to change the upper and lower angle limits. Wider sectors are easier to select.

3. Optional sector colors and numbers show the current choice during a pull. Direction stability prevents rapid switching near a divider.

4. Changing sector count remaps existing assignments. Check the resulting zone actions before trying the new layout.
Reach apps, actions, groups, and controls with a radial menu.

1. Add apps, shortcuts, actions, groups, or control modules to Pie control Set 1 or Set 2. Items can have their own hold actions and ring placement.

2. For slide selection, assign Pie control to a swipe-and-hold gesture, keep the finger down, move over an item, and release. Tap selection keeps the menu open for a tap.

3. Pause over a group to open its children. Optional app drawer, recent apps, volume, and brightness modules extend the menu.

4. Tune reach, arc angle, icon size, colors, opacity, group delay, item hold delay, and outside tap behavior. Keep open after actions is optional.
A compact panel combines volume, brightness, media, and quick actions.

1. Assign Quick tools to a gesture, then drag the volume or brightness slider or use media controls directly.

2. Add your preferred action items and reorder the volume, brightness, media, and actions sections.

3. Media progress and transport controls can be shown separately. Seek buttons move backward or forward by 15 seconds when the player supports seeking.

4. Choose panel colors, selected tool color, opacity, system accent syncing, and outside tap behavior. Drag the title to position the panel.
Search apps and pin the shortcuts you use most.

1. Assign App launcher and open it from an edge. Search by app name; package name searching is optional.

2. Pin apps or shortcuts in the launcher collection. Choose whether to show pinned items alongside all apps or only pinned items.

3. Set the number of columns, labels, icon pack, search visibility, and whether the keyboard opens automatically.

4. Keep open after actions and outside tap pass-through control how the launcher behaves after selection. App launches follow the normal unlock flow.
Artwork, expressive transport buttons, and responsive track seeking.

1. Assign Media controller or Notch media to open the active player. Use the large play/pause button or previous/next controls. Unavailable player commands are disabled.

2. Drag the seek slider to move within the track when seeking is supported. Time labels show the current position and total duration.

3. Assign Media seek to a hold gesture, then move left or right for continuous seeking. Seek sensitivity changes how far the track moves.

4. Theme, opacity, shaded artwork, progress visibility, and outside tap behavior are configurable. Media details follow lock screen and app privacy settings.
Clipboard, notes, and action tabs beside the current app.

1. Enable the clipboard, notes, and actions tabs you want. The selected tab can be remembered between openings.

2. Clipboard history is optional. Tap a clip to open Copy, Search, Translate, and Share actions, or enable Tap a clip to paste. Set the history limit and clear saved clips from the panel.

3. Add, edit, or delete notes, and add actions to the actions collection. Clips marked sensitive are skipped by default.

4. Panel contents follow lock screen and app-lock privacy. Configure theme, opacity, and outside tap behavior for a comfortable reading surface.
Browse notification cards, reply, snooze, and control media.

1. Assign Notification carousel to open current notifications. Swipe or use previous/next controls to browse cards. App filters and ongoing notifications are optional.

2. Open the notification, expand its content, dismiss clearable cards, or snooze for the selected duration. Clear all removes eligible notifications.

3. Reply appears only when the notification offers an inline reply action. Media notifications expose the commands supported by their player.

4. Content follows notification privacy and app-lock settings. Choose theme, opacity, background shading, and outside tap behavior.
Control a pointer from a comfortable thumb area.

1. Open Touch pad, then move within the pad to move the cursor across the current app. Tap to click at the cursor position.

2. Use double tap and drag for a swipe. Long press can replay a hold when enabled; timing, replay duration, and sensitivity are adjustable.

3. Pad width, opacity, cursor color, and outside tap pass-through control the presentation.

4. Input stays within the eligible app area, leaving system navigation and protected screen content available to their normal controls.
A movable thumb pad reaches content higher on the screen.

1. Open Remote cursor and drag the small pad to move the pointer. Tap the pad to click where the pointer is shown.

2. Choose double tap and hold actions, including a normal double click, replayed swipe, dismissal, or a custom action. Triple tap can reset the pointer.

3. Optional top edge shortcuts and flick-to-close add quick controls. Outside touch and inactivity settings determine dismissal.

4. Tune pad size, cursor size, speed, color, and opacity. Pointer input follows app, lock screen, and system navigation bounds.
Scroll a page automatically or control it with a held drag.

1. Assign Page scroll and choose Auto scroll or Hold and drag. Automatic scrolling opens controls for pause, speed, direction, and close.

2. For held dragging, keep the gesture or control held and move up or down to scroll through the page.

3. Scroll to top and Scroll to bottom jump to supported page boundaries. Speed has seven levels.

4. Scrolling stops when its app becomes unavailable or the controls are closed. Colors, opacity, and accent syncing match the rest of EdgeGo.
Train custom shapes and assign actions to them.

1. Record the same shape three times and assign an action. Matching confidence and direction sensitivity tune recognition.

2. Edge drawings begin in a configured edge zone and use one finger. The full drawing pad supports one to three fingers.

3. Use a clear shape with a turn for one-finger drawings. Keep all training samples consistent. Optional Hold at end waits before running the action.

4. Draw the trained shape and release, or hold at its end when required. The drawing pad closes after its timeout or a closing tap.
Reduce brightness further and schedule comfortable viewing.

1. Assign Extra dim to toggle the system dimming feature. Set intensity and optional warmth to suit the screen.

2. Enable start and stop schedules and choose their times. Each schedule can be controlled independently.

3. Screen blackout covers the display while the device remains active. Tap the blackout screen to leave it.

4. Brightness controls remain separate from extra dim, so their adjustments work with the selected display settings.
Top edge media, app sets, and a small timer.

1. Assign Notch media, Notch apps, or Notch timer to a gesture. Top edge offset places the trigger below the cutout when needed.

2. Notch apps has two item sets, or can share Pie control items. Add apps, shortcuts, and actions to the selected collection.

3. Start a timer from a quick duration or a minute value, then pause, resume, or stop it. A notification appears when the timer finishes.

4. Theme and opacity controls help these compact panels fit naturally beside the ROM status area.
Save complete gesture setups and move them between devices.

1. Save the current setup as a named preset. Apply a preset to restore its mappings and options, or update it with the current settings.

2. Assign Preset picker or an individual preset action to a gesture for quick switching.

3. Export a backup and choose its destination. Import a compatible EdgeGo backup to restore configuration, drawings, macros, and presets.

4. The preset picker has its own reach, opacity, names, and outside tap options. Review zone placement when the display size or orientation changes.
Record visible taps and swipes, edit steps, and replay in an app.

1. Create a named macro and choose its target app. Start Record taps and swipes, then interact with that app while the small recording toolbar remains visible.

2. The background stays clear during recording. Pause skips interactions; Save keeps the recorded steps. Stop discards the current unsaved recording.

3. Edit action, tap, swipe, and wait steps, including coordinates and duration. Run the macro from its settings or an assigned gesture.

4. Playback is tied to its target app and user. Touch outside the toolbar stops playback. Keyboard input is not recorded; leaving the app or locking the screen ends the session.
Automatically pause selected edges in the places you choose.

1. Add an app pause rule and select the edges to pause. Separate lock screen and launcher edge lists allow more precise control.

2. Use GameSpace, fullscreen, keyboard, and touch exploration protections in Behavior and timing. Paused edges remove their touch areas and indicators.

3. Tap through temporarily pauses one originating zone. Pause EdgeGo pauses the feature for a minute; its Quick Settings tile turns the feature on or off.

4. After a temporary pause expires, eligible zones return automatically. Disable an individual zone for a lasting change.
A reference for every built-in action and how to assign it.

1. Open a zone, choose a gesture, and select an action. Tap, swipe, hold, and extended mappings can each use different actions.

2. Up/down volume and brightness actions adjust repeatedly while a swipe or hold remains down. Slider actions track finger movement. Other single actions run once per gesture.

3. App, shortcut, group, macro, and preset selections are available in their pickers and collections. Locked actions follow the normal system unlock flow.

4. The entries below describe every built-in action. Commands depend on the relevant app or system feature being available.
